        # Save the workbook to the given filename
        wb.save(filename)

from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

# Define the base class for our models
Base = declarative_base()

# Define a base class for our models
class User(Base):
    # Define the table for our users
    __tablename__ = 'users'
    
    # Define the columns for our users
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    email = Column(String)

# Create an engine to connect to the database
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///example.db')

# Create all tables in the engine
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

# Create a session to interact with the database
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = Session()

# Define a function to add a new user
def add_user(name, email):
    # Create a new user object
    new_user = User(name=name, email=email)
    
    # Add the user to the session
    session.add(new_user)
    
    # Commit the changes to the database
    session.commit()

# Define a function to retrieve all users
def get_users():
    # Get all users from the session
    users = session.query(User).all()
    
    # Return the users
    return users

# Define a function to update an existing user
def update_user(id, name, email):
    # Get the user to update
    user = session.query(User).get(id)
    
    # If the user exists, update their name and email
    if user:
        user.name = name
        user.email = email
        
        # Commit the changes to the database
        session.commit()
    else:
        # If the user does not exist, raise an error
        raise ValueError("User not found")

# Define a function to delete a user
def delete_user(id):
    # Get the user to delete
    user = session.query(User).get(id)
    
    # If the user exists, delete it
    if user:
        session.delete(user)
        
        # Commit the changes to the database
        session.commit()
    else:
        # If the user does not exist, raise an error
        raise ValueError("User not found")

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Add a new user
    add_user("John Doe", "john@example.com")
    
    # Retrieve all users
    users = get_users()
    
    # Update an existing user
    update_user(1, "Jane Doe", "jane@example.com")
    
    # Delete a user
    delete_user(1)

def process_xml_file(xml_file_path):
    """
    Process an XML file using libxml2, libxslt, and ElementTree.
    
    Args:
        xml_file_path (str): The path to the XML file to process.
    """

    # Parse the XML file using ElementTree
    tree = ET.parse(xml_file_path)

    # Get the root element of the XML file
    root = tree.getroot()

    # Define a function to convert XML elements to strings
    def element_to_string(element):
        # Use the .text attribute to get the text content of the element
        # and the .attrib dictionary to get the attributes
        # and the .attrib.items() method to get a list of all attributes
        # and the .text.strip() method to remove any whitespace from the text
        return ' '.join(f'{key}="{value}"' if value is not None else key for key, value in element.attrib.items()) + ' ' + element.text.strip()

    # Process each element in the XML file
    for element in root.iter():
        # Convert the element to a string using the function defined above

        # Print the processed element string

from google.cloud import bigtable

    "path_to_your_service_account_key.json",

)

```
